Title: Verify that orders for a shop are displayed in descending order by creation date (newest first)
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop owner with at least 3 existing orders in the shop
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Orders' section in the shop dashboard. 2. Observe the list of orders displayed on the first page.

Test Data: Shop with orders created on: today, yesterday, and two days ago
Expected Result: The orders are listed with the most recently created order at the top of the list, followed by older orders in descending order by creation date.

Title: Verify pagination works correctly with newest orders appearing on the first page
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop owner with at least 15 existing orders in the shop, created over multiple days
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Orders' section in the shop dashboard. 2. Set the pagination size to 5 orders per page. 3. Observe the orders on the first page. 4. Navigate to the second page and observe the orders.

Test Data: Shop with 15 orders created over the last 30 days, pagination size set to 5
Expected Result: The first page displays the 5 most recently created orders. The second page displays the next 5 most recent orders, and so on, all in descending order by creation date.

Title: Attempt to fetch orders for a shop with an invalid shop ID format
Preconditions: User is logged in as a SHOP_OWNER with a bound shop
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Orders' section in the shop dashboard. 2. Manually modify the URL to replace the shop ID with a non-numeric value (e.g., 'abc'). 3. Press Enter to load the page.

Test Data: Shop ID: 'abc' (non-numeric)
Expected Result: The system displays an error message indicating that the 'Shop ID' must be a valid numeric value. No orders are displayed.

Title: Attempt to fetch orders for a non-existent shop ID
Preconditions: User is logged in as a SHOP_OWNER with a bound shop
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Orders' section in the shop dashboard. 2. Manually modify the URL to replace the shop ID with a numeric value that does not correspond to any existing shop (e.g., '999999'). 3. Press Enter to load the page.

Test Data: Shop ID: 999999 (non-existent)
Expected Result: The system displays an error message indicating that no orders exist for the specified shop ID. No orders are displayed.

Title: Attempt to fetch orders for a shop without authentication
Preconditions: User is not logged in
Steps:
1. Open a browser in incognito mode. 2. Navigate directly to the URL for fetching orders by shop ID (e.g., '/shops/1/orders'). 3. Press Enter to load the page.

Test Data: Shop ID: 1 (valid but unauthenticated access)
Expected Result: The system returns an HTTP 401 Unauthorized status code with an error message indicating that authentication is required. No orders are displayed.

Title: Attempt to fetch orders for a shop as an unauthorized user (non-SHOP_OWNER role)
Preconditions: User is logged in with a role other than SHOP_OWNER (e.g., CUSTOMER)
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Orders' section in the shop dashboard. 2. The system should either hide the option or display an error when accessed.

Test Data: User role: CUSTOMER
Expected Result: The system returns an HTTP 403 Forbidden status code with an error message indicating that the user is not authorized to view orders for this shop. No orders are displayed.

Title: Attempt to fetch orders for a shop with invalid pagination parameters (negative page number)

Test Data: Page: -1, Limit: 10
Expected Result: The system displays an error message indicating that the 'page' parameter must be a non-negative integer. No orders are displayed.

Title: Attempt to fetch orders for a shop with a non-integer pagination parameter

Steps:
1. Navigate to the Orders section in the dashboard. 2. Select the 'All Orders' tab. 3. Observe the list of orders displayed.

Test Data: shopId = [valid shop ID with no orders]
Expected Result: The system displays a message 'No orders found' and an empty list with no errors.

Title: Verify that the order listing for a shop is sorted by creation date in descending order to prevent data manipulation via reordering
Preconditions: User is logged in as SHOP_OWNER with access to at least two orders for their shop, created at different times (e.g., Order A created yesterday, Order B created today).
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Orders' section in the shop dashboard. 2. Observe the order of the listed orders. 3. Verify that the most recently created order (Order B) appears first in the list.

Test Data: Order A (created: 2023-10-01T10:00:00), Order B (created: 2023-10-02T10:00:00)
Expected Result: The order list displays Order B (created today) at the top, followed by Order A (created yesterday). The sorting is consistent and not affected by other fields (e.g., order ID, customer name).

Title: Verify that a SHOP_OWNER cannot access or infer the existence of orders from another shop by manipulating the shop ID in the order listing
Preconditions: User is logged in as SHOP_OWNER of Shop A. Another shop (Shop B) exists with at least one order.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Orders' section in the shop dashboard. 2. Using browser developer tools or a proxy, intercept the request to fetch orders and modify the shop ID parameter to Shop B's ID. 3. Observe the response or UI behavior.

Test Data: Shop A ID: 1001, Shop B ID: 1002
Expected Result: The system displays a generic error message (e.g., 'Access denied' or 'No orders found'). No orders from Shop B are displayed, and the response does not indicate whether Shop B exists or has orders.
